library(nlmixr2lib)
library(PKNCA)
library(rxode2)

library(ggplot2)

# Models and source

Wang 2025 links aripiprazole exposure to the time to recurrence of any mood
episode in adults with bipolar I disorder maintained on aripiprazole once
monthly (AOM). The analysis has two layers:

1. **Exposure.** The previously published population PK model of Wang 2022
   was applied, with every parameter fixed, to the bipolar trial. It is
   already in the library as `modellib("Wang_2022_aripiprazole")`, and the
   supplement's Table S2 reproduces it verbatim, so this paper adds no PK
   parameters.
2. **Exposure-response.** Two Cox proportional-hazards models were fitted
   separately to the same 265 patients: the final model, with the predicted
   concentration as a continuous linear predictor, and a categorical model
   that tests the 95 ng/mL threshold established in schizophrenia. They are
   packaged as two files:

* `Wang_2025_aripiprazole_recurrence` (continuous, final):
  `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2025_aripiprazole_recurrence"))$description`
* `Wang_2025_aripiprazole_recurrence_cutoff` (categorical):
  `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2025_aripiprazole_recurrence_cutoff"))$description`
* Citation: `r rxode2::rxode(readModelDb("Wang_2025_aripiprazole_recurrence"))$reference`
* Article: <https://doi.org/10.1002/cpdd.1580>

The sibling schizophrenia analysis from the same group is
`modellib("Wang_2022_aripiprazole_relapse")`. There the exposure-response model
was an exponential (constant-hazard) model with the 95 ng/mL threshold, and the
hazard ratio was 1/4.41.

# Population

Data come from the phase 3 trial NCT01567527 of AOM 400 mg as maintenance
treatment in bipolar I disorder (Wang 2025 Methods; Appendix S1). Patients
entered in a manic episode (YMRS >= 20). They were converted to oral
aripiprazole and stabilised on it (Phases A and B), then stabilised on
open-label AOM 400 mg every 4 weeks, with oral aripiprazole 10 or 15 mg/day for
the first 14 days (Phase C, 12-28 weeks). Finally they were randomised 1:1 to
continue AOM or switch to placebo injections for 52 weeks (Phase D). A single
decrease to AOM 300 mg was allowed for tolerability, and 68 patients (16.2%)
used it.

The exposure-response set is the 265 patients of Phase D: 132 on AOM and 133 on
placebo (Table S5). Their mean (SD) age was 40.1 (11.0) years and their body
mass index 30.2 (7.2) kg/m^2. 57.4% were female. By race, 54.3% were White,
27.9% Black or African American and 14.0% Asian. Mean MADRS and YMRS totals at
randomisation were 2.7 and 2.8. The population PK validation set was larger, at
420 patients (Table S3). In that set, 2.9% were CYP2D6 poor metabolisers and
6.4% had an inconclusive or missing genotype. There were 103 recurrences: 35
(26.5%) on AOM and 68 (51.1%) on placebo (Table 1).

The exposure metric, `Ctau` in the paper and `CTROUGH` here, is the
model-predicted aripiprazole plasma concentration 672 h (28 days) after the
first Phase D injection. Placebo patients received no active drug at that
injection, but they were still washing out their last open-label AOM dose,
given about 1344 h (56 days) before the landmark. So their `CTROUGH` is
substantial and not zero.

# Source trace

| Model element | Value | Source location |
|---|---|---|
| Continuous model equation `S(t) = S0(t)^exp(beta * Ctau)` | -- | Appendix S4, step 5 |
| `e_ctrough_haz` | -0.00346 (RSE 44%) | Results, "Exposure-Response Model" (HR 0.99655, 95% CI 0.9936-0.9995, P = .0230) |
| Linear rather than log-linear Ctau | -- | Results (linear P = .0170 in univariate testing) |
| No retained covariates (age, BMI, MADRS, YMRS, sex, race screened) | -- | Results; Appendix S4, step 3 |
| `ctrough_cut` | 95 ng/mL (fixed) | Results, "Exposure-Response Model" (tested, not estimated) |
| `e_ctrough_cut_haz` | log(0.6450) | Results, "Exposure-Response Model" (HR 0.6450, 95% CI 0.4372-0.9514, P = .0270) |
| Ctau definition (672 h after the first Phase D dose) | -- | Methods, "Development of the Exposure-Response Model" |
| Upstream PK model | `Wang_2022_aripiprazole` | Methods; Appendix S2, Table S2 |
| Ctau mean (SD) by arm | AOM 170.5 (71.6); placebo 78.7 (36.1) ng/mL | Results text; Table 1 |
| Ctau quartile edges, pooled | 9.48 / 70.39 / 110.21 / 164.2 / 390.86 ng/mL | Figure 2 legend |
| N below / at or above 95 ng/mL | 111 / 154 | Figure 3 panel labels |

# Model structure

Both models return the relative hazard `hr = exp(lhr)`. In the continuous
model the reference is a hypothetical patient with `CTROUGH = 0`. In the
categorical model it is the group below 95 ng/mL. A Cox regression leaves the
baseline hazard `h0(t)` unspecified, and the paper reports no estimate of it.
So neither file offers a survivor function. To get a patient's hazard,
multiply `hr` by a baseline the user supplies.

# Validation

## A. The published hazard ratios are reproduced exactly

Both models are deterministic and algebraic, so their output can be checked
against the printed numbers to the printed precision.

```{r hr-eval}
# One observation row per grid point on a single subject, with the covariate
# as an event-table column. A params data.frame would be read as one row per
# subject and fail on a one-subject event table.
erEval <- function(model, grid) {
  ev <- data.frame(id = 1L, time = seq_along(grid), amt = 0, evid = 0L,
                   CTROUGH = grid)
  s <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(model, events = ev,
                                     returnType = "data.frame"))
  stopifnot(nrow(s) == length(grid))
  s$hr
}

modCont <- readModelDb("Wang_2025_aripiprazole_recurrence")
modCut  <- readModelDb("Wang_2025_aripiprazole_recurrence_cutoff")

hrPer1 <- erEval(modCont, c(0, 1))
hrCut  <- erEval(modCut, c(0, 94.99, 95, 400))

# Continuous model: per-1 ng/mL hazard ratio is printed as 0.99655, and the
# derived per-1 ng/mL reduction as 0.34%.
coefCont <- -0.00346
seCont   <- 0.44 * abs(coefCont)   # RSE 44%
ciCont   <- exp(coefCont + c(-1, 1) * qnorm(0.975) * seCont)

hrTable <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("HR per 1 ng/mL Ctau", "Hazard reduction per 1 ng/mL (%)",
               "95% CI lower (from RSE)", "95% CI upper (from RSE)",
               "HR, Ctau >= 95 vs < 95 ng/mL", "Fold reduction, 1/HR",
               "Risk reduction, 1 - HR (%)"),
  model = c(hrPer1[2] / hrPer1[1], 100 * (1 - hrPer1[2] / hrPer1[1]),
            ciCont[1], ciCont[2],
            hrCut[3] / hrCut[2], hrCut[2] / hrCut[3],
            100 * (1 - hrCut[3] / hrCut[2])),
  published = c(0.99655, 0.34, 0.9936, 0.9995, 0.6450, 1.55, 36)
)
hrTable |>
  dplyr::mutate(model = signif(model, 5)) |>
  dplyr::rename("Quantity" = quantity, "Packaged model" = model,
                "Wang 2025" = published) |>
  knitr::kable()

stopifnot(
  # Exact reproduction, rounded to the printed precision.
  round(hrPer1[2] / hrPer1[1], 5) == 0.99655,
  # 0.345% printed as 0.34%: truncated, not rounded, hence the 0.01 window.
  abs(100 * (1 - hrPer1[2] / hrPer1[1]) - 0.34) < 0.01,
  all(abs(ciCont - c(0.9936, 0.9995)) < 1e-4),
  abs(hrCut[3] / hrCut[2] - 0.6450) < 1e-10,
  round(hrCut[2] / hrCut[3], 2) == 1.55,
  # 35.5% printed as 36%: within half a percentage point.
  abs(100 * (1 - hrCut[3] / hrCut[2]) - 36) <= 0.5 + 1e-9,
  # The threshold is a step: no effect just below 95, full effect at 95 and above.
  hrCut[1] == 1, hrCut[2] == 1, hrCut[3] == hrCut[4]
)
```

The reported per-1 ng/mL reduction of 0.34% is `1 - 0.99655 = 0.345%`,
truncated. The 36% risk reduction is `1 - 0.6450 = 35.5%`, rounded. The 95% CI
recomputed from the printed RSE (44%) matches the printed 0.9936-0.9995 to four
decimals. This checks the coefficient and its precision together.

```{r hr-curve, fig.cap = "Relative hazard of recurrence of any mood episode against aripiprazole Ctau for the continuous (final) and categorical Wang 2025 models. Dotted lines mark the pooled Ctau quartile edges printed in the Figure 2 legend of Wang 2025."}
grid <- seq(0, 400, by = 1)
curves <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  tibble::tibble(CTROUGH = grid, hr = erEval(modCont, grid),
                 model = "Continuous (final): reference Ctau = 0"),
  tibble::tibble(CTROUGH = grid, hr = erEval(modCut, grid),
                 model = "Categorical 95 ng/mL: reference Ctau < 95")
)
ggplot(curves, aes(CTROUGH, hr, colour = model)) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = c(70.39, 110.21, 164.2), linetype = "dotted",
             colour = "grey50") +
  geom_line(linewidth = 0.9) +
  labs(x = "Aripiprazole Ctau (ng/mL)", y = "Relative hazard of recurrence",
       colour = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

The two models agree in direction but differ in what they say about patients
above the threshold. Across the inter-quartile range of Ctau (70 to 164 ng/mL),
the continuous model's hazard falls to
`r signif(exp(-0.00346 * (164.2 - 70.39)), 3)` times its value at the lower
edge. The categorical model applies
its single 0.645 step at 95 ng/mL and nothing beyond.

## B. The exposure driver: reproducing Ctau with the upstream PK model

`CTROUGH` is an input to both models. Wang 2025 generated it from each
patient's recorded dosing history and empirical-Bayes parameters under the
Wang 2022 PK model. The individual records are not published. Below, a virtual
trial is run through `Wang_2022_aripiprazole` with the protocol's dosing
schedule, and its predicted Ctau is compared with the published summaries.
This checks that the column a user would generate with the library's PK model
lies on the same scale as the one these coefficients were fitted on.

```{r cohort}
# rxSetSeed() fixes rxode2's draws within one rxode2 build. The assertions
# below are on means and central quantiles, never on cohort extremes.
set.seed(20251101)
rxode2::rxSetSeed(20251101)

nPerArm <- 200L
bmiMean <- 30.2
bmiSd   <- 7.2
bmiSdlog <- sqrt(log(1 + (bmiSd / bmiMean)^2))

makeSubjects <- function(n, idOffset, arm) {
  tibble::tibble(
    id = idOffset + seq_len(n),
    arm = arm,
    SEXF = as.numeric(stats::runif(n) < 0.574),
    BMI = stats::rlnorm(n, log(bmiMean) - bmiSdlog^2 / 2, bmiSdlog),
    # 12 poor metabolisers among the 393 with a known phenotype (Table S3).
    CYP2D6_PM = as.numeric(stats::runif(n) < 12 / 393),
    CONMED_CYP2D6_INH = 0,
    CONMED_CYP3A4_INH = 0,
    STUDY_ARI_PHASE3 = 1,
    oralPhaseC = ifelse(stats::runif(n) < 0.5, 10, 15)
  )
}
subjects <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  makeSubjects(nPerArm, 0L, "AOM 400 mg"),
  makeSubjects(nPerArm, nPerArm, "Placebo")
)

tau   <- 672        # AOM dosing interval (h)
tC0   <- 42 * 24    # Phase C starts after 6 weeks of oral 15 mg QD (Phase B)
tD0   <- tC0 + 4 * tau  # first Phase D injection, after 4 Phase C AOM doses
tCtau <- tD0 + tau      # the Ctau landmark

# Oral doses use rate = -1 so the model's zero-order input R1 applies; AOM
# doses are bolus records into depot2. The placebo arm receives no Phase D
# dose. Observations are on the central ODE state.
doses <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  subjects |> dplyr::mutate(time = 0, amt = 15, cmt = "depot", rate = -1,
                            ii = 24, addl = 41L),
  subjects |> dplyr::mutate(time = tC0, amt = oralPhaseC, cmt = "depot",
                            rate = -1, ii = 24, addl = 13L),
  subjects |> dplyr::mutate(time = tC0, amt = 400, cmt = "depot2", rate = 0,
                            ii = tau, addl = 3L),
  subjects |> dplyr::filter(arm == "AOM 400 mg") |>
    dplyr::mutate(time = tD0, amt = 400, cmt = "depot2", rate = 0, ii = 0,
                  addl = 0L)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(evid = 1L)
obs <- subjects |>
  tidyr::expand_grid(time = seq(tD0, tCtau, by = 24)) |>
  dplyr::mutate(amt = 0, cmt = "central", rate = 0, ii = 0, addl = 0L,
                evid = 0L)
events <- dplyr::bind_rows(doses, obs) |>
  dplyr::select(-oralPhaseC) |>
  dplyr::arrange(id, time, dplyr::desc(evid))

stopifnot(
  !anyDuplicated(events[events$evid == 0L, c("id", "time")]),
  nPerArm <= 200L
)
```

```{r simulate}
modPk <- readModelDb("Wang_2022_aripiprazole")
simPk <- as.data.frame(rxode2::rxSolve(modPk, events = events, keep = "arm",
                                       returnType = "data.frame"))
ctau <- simPk |>
  dplyr::filter(time == tCtau) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, arm, CTROUGH = Cc)
stopifnot(nrow(ctau) == 2L * nPerArm)
```

```{r ctau-arm}
ctauArm <- ctau |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(mean = mean(CTROUGH), sd = stats::sd(CTROUGH),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::mutate(pubMean = c(170.5, 78.7), pubSd = c(71.6, 36.1),
                pctDiff = 100 * (mean - pubMean) / pubMean)
ctauArm |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(mean, sd, pctDiff), \(x) round(x, 1))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "Simulated mean" = mean, "Simulated SD" = sd,
                "Published mean" = pubMean, "Published SD" = pubSd,
                "Mean difference (%)" = pctDiff) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Ctau by arm: virtual trial vs Wang 2025 Results and Table 1 (ng/mL).")

pooledQ <- stats::quantile(ctau$CTROUGH, c(0.25, 0.5, 0.75))
qTable <- tibble::tibble(
  quantity = c("25th percentile", "Median", "75th percentile",
               "Fraction below 95 ng/mL"),
  simulated = c(unname(pooledQ), mean(ctau$CTROUGH < 95)),
  published = c(70.39, 110.21, 164.2, 111 / 265)
) |>
  dplyr::mutate(pctDiff = 100 * (simulated - published) / published)
qTable |>
  dplyr::mutate(dplyr::across(c(simulated, published, pctDiff),
                              \(x) signif(x, 3))) |>
  dplyr::rename("Pooled Ctau" = quantity, "Virtual trial" = simulated,
                "Wang 2025" = published, "Difference (%)" = pctDiff) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Pooled Ctau quartiles (Figure 2 legend) and the share below 95 ng/mL (Figure 3: 111 of 265).")

stopifnot(
  # Structural: a mis-specified dose, interval or landmark (for example Ctau
  # read at the Phase D dose instead of 672 h later, which is identical for
  # the AOM arm but doubles the placebo value) moves these by tens of percent.
  all(abs(ctauArm$pctDiff) < 20),
  all(abs(qTable$pctDiff[1:3]) < 20),
  abs(qTable$simulated[4] - qTable$published[4]) < 0.10
)
```

The virtual trial lands within about 10% of every published summary. It sits
slightly high, which matches the bias the paper reports when it applied this PK
model to the bipolar data: a median population prediction error of -10.1%
(observed below predicted) over all samples, and -2.0% in Phase D only
(Table S4). The virtual trial also gives every AOM patient 400 mg, whereas
16.2% of the real cohort used 300 mg for part of the time.

## C. PKNCA summary of the first double-blind interval

PKNCA does not apply to the Cox models themselves, which take no dose. It does
apply to the exposure interval that defines `CTROUGH`. `clast.obs` over
`[tD0, tD0 + 672 h]` is Ctau. It must equal the Ctau extracted above, which
checks the landmark arithmetic.

```{r pknca}
concPk <- simPk |>
  dplyr::filter(!is.na(Cc)) |>
  dplyr::transmute(id, arm, time, Cc)
concObj <- PKNCA::PKNCAconc(concPk, Cc ~ time | arm + id)
intervals <- data.frame(start = tD0, end = tCtau, cmax = TRUE, cmin = TRUE,
                        cav = TRUE, clast.obs = TRUE)
ncaRes <- PKNCA::pk.nca(PKNCA::PKNCAdata(concObj, intervals = intervals))
ncaWide <- as.data.frame(ncaRes) |>
  dplyr::select(arm, id, PPTESTCD, PPORRES) |>
  tidyr::pivot_wider(names_from = PPTESTCD, values_from = PPORRES)

ncaWide |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(dplyr::across(c(cmax, cmin, cav, clast.obs),
                                 \(x) round(stats::median(x), 1)),
                   .groups = "drop") |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm, "Cmax" = cmax, "Cmin" = cmin, "Cav" = cav,
                "Ctau (clast.obs)" = clast.obs) |>
  knitr::kable(caption = "Median NCA over the first Phase D interval (ng/mL), virtual trial.")

chk <- dplyr::inner_join(ncaWide, ctau, by = c("arm", "id"))
stopifnot(
  nrow(chk) == 2L * nPerArm,
  # Same simulated values, so the agreement is exact up to floating point.
  max(abs(chk$clast.obs - chk$CTROUGH)) < 1e-8
)
```

In the placebo arm, the interval minimum is the Ctau itself: the concentration
only washes out. In the AOM arm, the median interval minimum lies a few percent
below the median Ctau. For this formulation, the end-of-interval value is
close to the interval minimum but not identical to it.

## D. Relative hazard across the virtual trial

```{r hr-cohort}
ctau$hrCont <- erEval(modCont, ctau$CTROUGH)
ctau$hrCut  <- erEval(modCut, ctau$CTROUGH)

ctau |>
  dplyr::group_by(arm) |>
  dplyr::summarise(
    `Median Ctau (ng/mL)` = round(stats::median(CTROUGH), 1),
    `Geometric mean hr, continuous` = signif(exp(mean(log(hrCont))), 3),
    `Share at or above 95 ng/mL` = round(mean(CTROUGH >= 95), 2),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  dplyr::rename("Arm" = arm) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

```{r ctau-hist, fig.cap = "Distribution of simulated Ctau by arm, with the 95 ng/mL threshold of the categorical model. Compare with the pooled quartile edges of Wang 2025 Figure 2 (70.39, 110.21 and 164.2 ng/mL)."}
ggplot(ctau, aes(CTROUGH, fill = arm)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 20, alpha = 0.6, position = "identity",
                 boundary = 0) +
  geom_vline(xintercept = 95, linetype = "dashed") +
  labs(x = "Simulated aripiprazole Ctau (ng/mL)", y = "Patients", fill = NULL) +
  theme_bw() +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom")
```

At the arm means, the continuous model gives the AOM arm a hazard about
`r signif(exp(-0.00346 * (170.5 - 78.7)), 2)` times that of the placebo arm,
from the published means 170.5 and 78.7 ng/mL. This is a much smaller contrast
than the observed recurrence fractions (26.5% vs 51.1%) suggest. Part of the
reason is that the single Ctau value is fixed per patient: in the placebo arm,
exposure keeps falling after the landmark and the model cannot see it.
Readers who want the treatment-arm contrast should not read it off these
models.

# Assumptions and deviations

- **No baseline hazard.** Both models are semiparametric Cox regressions. The
  baseline survival `S0(t)` is unspecified by the method, and Wang 2025 does
  not report it. The models therefore return the relative hazard only, and
  Figure 3 (the survival VPC) cannot be reproduced. The maintainers did not
  build a parametric baseline from the Kaplan-Meier curves in Figures 2 and 3,
  because it would not come from the fit.
- **The categorical HR is printed, its coefficient is not.**
  `e_ctrough_cut_haz` is `log(0.6450) = -0.4385`. The log-scale midpoint of
  the printed 95% CI, -0.4386, confirms it.
- **The 95 ng/mL threshold is fixed.** It was carried over from the
  schizophrenia analysis and tested, not estimated, so it is wrapped in
  `fixed()`.
- **Screened covariates.** Age, BMI, baseline MADRS, baseline YMRS, sex and
  race were tested in a full model with backward elimination (P < 0.01 to
  retain), and none was retained. No estimates are reported. They are listed
  in `covariatesDataExcluded` of the continuous model for provenance. That list
  names the YMRS score `SCORE_YMRS`, after the registered `SCORE_MADRS`. The
  name is not a registered canonical and is documentation only.
- **Virtual-trial design, used for Section B only.** It has 6 weeks of oral
  15 mg QD (Phase B), then 4 open-label AOM 400 mg doses with oral 10 or 15 mg
  for the first 14 days (Phase C, the protocol minimum). The AOM arm then
  gets the first Phase D injection, and Ctau is read 672 h later. BMI is
  log-normal with the Table S5 mean and SD. The female share is 57.4%. The
  CYP2D6 poor-metaboliser share is 12/393 among the known phenotypes, and no
  patient takes a CYP inhibitor. The real Phase C lasted 12-28 weeks, and
  16.2% of patients stepped down to 300 mg. The trial's $MIX assignment of
  unknown CYP2D6 phenotypes is not reproduced.
- **Table 1 placebo Ctau row is internally inconsistent.** Table 1 gives the
  placebo arm's mean (SD) Ctau as 16.4 (42.6) ng/mL for censored patients
  (n = 65) and 52.6 (58.6) ng/mL for patients with an event (n = 68), but
  78.7 (36.1) ng/mL overall. The overall figure is larger than both subgroup
  means, so the three cannot all be right. The overall 78.7 ng/mL is repeated
  in the Results text, and it agrees with the washout predicted by the PK
  model (Section B). So Section B compares against the overall values. The AOM row is
  also not exactly self-consistent: the count-weighted mean of 187.2 and 163.3
  is 180.9, against 170.5 printed. Only the printed overall means are used.
- **Time unit.** The models have no time dependence. The source analysis
  measured follow-up in days from randomisation, up to about 380 days
  (Figures 1-3).
